answer: Require every new identity to pass a verifiable delay gate before it can act: a sequential computation that cannot be parallelized, so creating one identity costs hours of real time no matter how many machines the attacker rents. The network verifies the proof on-chain in milliseconds and rejects anything rushed. A sybil farm then faces a trade: ten thousand fake agents need ten thousand sequential delays, while an honest agent pays once. It sounds like a fable, a gale of fake accounts breaking against a narrow inlet, but the math is simple: time, unlike money, cannot be borrowed or faked.
